column1: # suite-pole-baseline.tsv -- the fixture suite's POLE, and the only figure that decides how
# long `git push` takes. Read by scripts/validate-suite-pole.sh at pre-push.
# WHAT A LOADED FIGURE IS, AND WHY NOTHING ELSE MAY BE PUT HERE. The number below is the cost
# of one fixture directory measured WHILE THE WHOLE POOL WAS RUNNING -- twelve workers on this
# box, every fixture dispatched. The same unit driven alone gives a completely different
# number: one shard has measured 442s loaded against 112s solo. A solo timing and a loaded
# timing are not two readings of one quantity and must never be written into the same row.
# WHY ONE ROW. The suite is POLE-BOUND: its wall clock tracks the single longest DIRECTORY,
# not the sum over the pool. A file with a row per fixture is a file every push edits and
# nobody reads, and the rows for units that are not the pole rot in place. The guard refuses a
# second data row for that reason.
# THE RATCHET RULE. The row moves DOWN freely -- a faster suite needs no ceremony. It moves UP
# only as a reviewed edit carrying a MEASUREMENT and the load average it was taken under, in
# the same change as whatever made the suite slower, appended to the history below. A loaded
# box is not a reason to raise the row; re-run the gate, which is what the band is for.
# `# band:` is the percent of growth tolerated above the row before the push fails. It is the
# calibrated run-to-run spread plus stated headroom -- not a number chosen for comfort.
# `# jobs:` is the pool width the figure was taken under; the guard SKIPS rather than compares
# when the running width differs, because a different width is a different measurement.
# `# fixtures:` is the fixture-directory count of the tree the figure was taken on. It is
# reported and never compared -- it is there so a later reader can see whether the suite has
# grown under the figure.
# CALIBRATION -- THREE SERIAL FULL RUNS OF `AI_DLC_FIXTURE_NO_SKIP=1 bash .githooks/pre-push`
# ON AN UNCHANGED TREE, in a file:// clone of origin/main at 83747ef4, pool 12, 201 fixture
# directories, durations seeded from the operator clone's record so all three dispatch in the
# same longest-first order:
#   run 1: ledger-reverify 628s, wall 743s, load average 50.56 at start, gate green 21/21
#   run 2: ledger-reverify 563s, wall 629s, load average  9.06 at start, gate RED on one
#          unrelated fixture (agent-definition-render mutant-attribution flake); the durations
#          file was complete at 201 rows, so the pole figure is a full-dispatch reading
#   run 3: ledger-reverify 562s, wall 627s, load average  5.30 at start, gate green 21/21
# The next four rows moved together and in the same direction across all three, which is what
# says the spread is LOAD and not one unit misbehaving: reconcile-emit-report 377/325/325,
# gate-adjudication-mutants 330/291/287, check-24-adversarial-convergence 246/186/192,
# self-update-gate 226/196/197.
# HOW THE ROW AND THE BAND WERE DERIVED. n=3 under uncontrolled load gives no dispersion
# estimate; what it gives is an OBSERVED LOADED CEILING, and that is what the row is -- the MAX
# of the three, 628, not the mean and not the quiet-box figure. Taking the minimum would put
# the baseline under two of the three readings of an unchanged tree, which is a red on every
# busy push. The band is the observed spread, ceil((628-562)/562*100) = 12 percent, plus 8
# points of stated headroom = 20. Ceiling therefore 628 + ceil(628*20/100) = 754: a run at 754
# passes and a run at 755 fails.
# WHAT THIS ROW IS NOT COMPARABLE TO. Prior readings of this same row on other days, from the
# merged-forward `.git/ai-dlc-fixture-durations` record, were 490, 493 and 573 -- rows of mixed
# vintage, each a floor of unknown age. They are not three measurements of one quantity either,
# which is why the calibration above was run rather than read off the record.
# RATCHET HISTORY -- one line per change to the row, with its measurement and the load beside it.
#   v0.583.0  ledger-reverify 628  band 20  jobs 12  fixtures 201  (max of 628/563/562, loads 50.56/9.06/5.30)
# band: 20
# jobs: 12
# fixtures: 201
ledger-reverify 628
